facts: • The agreement delimited the boundary in the northern area between China and Pakistan. • The Karakoram Highway later improved road connectivity between the two countries.

question: Where did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests?
answer: At Ras Koh Hills in Chagai District, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998; further tests followed at Kharan on 30 May.
facts: • The tests of 28 May are commemorated as Youm-e-Takbeer. • Pakistan conducted its tests after India tested nuclear devices in May 1998.

question: A question claims Pakistan has a 1,200-mile border with which country. Is that accurate?
answer: The claim is inaccurate for Afghanistan: the Pakistan-Afghanistan border is generally estimated at about 2,640 km (1,640 miles), though sources vary.
facts: • The border is called the Durand Line. • Do not memorize “1,200 miles” as the accepted length of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

question: Basel is a city in which country?
answer: Switzerland.
facts: • Basel lies on the Rhine River near the French and German borders. • It is an important centre for the pharmaceutical and chemical industries.

question: What is the smallest continent?
answer: Australia, in the traditional seven-continent model.
facts: • Oceania is a wider geographic region that includes Australia, New Zealand and Pacific islands. • The answer can differ if a course treats “Oceania” as the continental region.

question: What is Pakistan's highest civil award?
answer: Nishan-e-Pakistan.
facts: • It is Pakistan's highest civilian award. • It may be conferred on Pakistani citizens and foreign nationals for distinguished service.

question: Who was Pakistan's first woman Governor-General?
answer: Pakistan has never had a woman Governor-General. Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan was Pakistan's first woman governor; she served as Governor of Sindh from 1973 to 1976.
facts: • Muhammad Ali Jinnah was Pakistan's first Governor-General. • Governor-General was a federal office abolished when Pakistan became a republic in 1956.

question: Who was Pakistan's second Prime Minister?
answer: Khawaja Nazimuddin.
facts: • He served from 1951 to 1953 after Liaquat Ali Khan's assassination. • Nazimuddin had earlier been Governor-General of Pakistan.

question: What is an empty set?
answer: A set with no elements; it is a finite set with cardinality zero.
facts: • It is represented by ∅ or {}. • The empty set is a subset of every set.

question: When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur?
answer: 4 February 1922 (some exam keys give 5 February; the commonly recorded date is 4 February).
facts: • The incident occurred in the Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces, British India. • Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement after the violence.

question: What is the longest river in Asia?
answer: The Yangtze River in China.
facts: • It is about 6,300 km long, depending on measurement. • The Yangtze flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai.

question: What does “Al-Saffah” mean?
answer: It is commonly translated as “the blood-shedder” or “one who sheds blood”; “top of a mountain” is not the standard historical meaning in this context.
facts: • Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah was the first Abbasid caliph. • The Abbasid Caliphate overthrew the Umayyads in 750 CE.

question: What is the nisab of gold for zakat?
answer: A commonly used Hanafi measure is 7.5 tola, approximately 87.48 grams of gold; published conversions may vary slightly.
facts: • Zakat on qualifying wealth is commonly 2.5% after one lunar year, subject to the relevant conditions. • Gold purity, local religious guidance and calculation conventions should be checked for personal zakat.

question: On what date did the 1857 uprising begin at Meerut?
facts: • The uprising at Meerut spread toward Delhi. • It is called the Indian Rebellion of 1857, the Revolt of 1857 or the First War of Independence in different traditions.

question: What was Hazrat Hamza's relationship to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
answer: He was the Prophet's paternal uncle and a companion; Islamic tradition also identifies them as foster brothers.
facts: • Hamza (RA) was martyred at the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH. • He is known by the honorific “Asadullah” (Lion of Allah) in Muslim tradition.

question: Which words can be synonyms of “prescribe”?
answer: Order, direct or specify; in medicine, it can mean to authorize a treatment or medicine.
facts: • “Prescribe” and “proscribe” have opposite meanings: prescribe means recommend/order; proscribe means forbid. • Choose the synonym that best fits the sentence.

question: What is the cube root of −2?
answer: −∛2 ≈ −1.2599; −1.25 is only a rough, inaccurate approximation.
facts: • The cube root of a negative real number is negative. • Since 1.26³ is approximately 2, ∛2 is about 1.26.

question: When was the Quit India Movement launched?
answer: 8 August 1942 (the mass movement began on 9 August after the leaders were arrested).
facts: • The All-India Congress Committee adopted the Quit India resolution in Bombay. • Mahatma Gandhi gave the “Do or Die” call.

question: Who is known by the title “Kaleemullah”?
answer: Prophet Musa (Moses), peace be upon him.
facts: • The title refers to his speaking with Allah, as described in Islamic tradition. • Other traditional titles include Khalilullah for Prophet Ibrahim and Ruhullah for Prophet Isa.

question: Who is the Speaker of Pakistan's National Assembly?
answer: Sardar Ayaz Sadiq (as listed by the National Assembly on 14 October 2026).
facts: • He was elected Speaker on 1 March 2024. • Asad Qaiser was a former Speaker, serving from 2018 to 2022.

question: What is 90% of 90?
facts: • 10% of 90 is 9; 90% is 9 × 9 = 81. • Percentage means “per hundred”.

question: What are some historical names used for India?
answer: Names include Bharat/Bharatavarsha, Hindustan and India, depending on language and historical context; there is no single answer that fits every period.
facts: • “Bharat” is used in India's constitutional text alongside “India”. • “Hindustan” has been used historically in Persianate and South Asian contexts.

question: “Israel” is a traditional title/name associated with which prophet?
answer: Prophet Yaqub (Jacob), peace be upon him, is traditionally identified as Israel.
facts: • Bani Israel means the Children of Israel. • The biblical/Quranic name traditions have some differences in formulation.

question: Which region lies between Pakistan and Tajikistan?
answer: The Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan lies between Pakistan and Tajikistan; Pakistan and Tajikistan do not share a direct border.
facts: • The corridor is part of Afghanistan's Badakhshan Province. • It separates Pakistan's northern areas from Tajikistan.

question: What are Laat and Uzza?
answer: Pre-Islamic Arabian deities/idols, commonly spelled al-Lat and al-Uzza.
facts: • They are mentioned in Surah An-Najm (53:19–20). • The third deity named in those verses is Manat.

question: Who was Pakistan's first Foreign Minister?
answer: Sir Muhammad Zafrullah Khan.
facts: • He was Pakistan's first foreign minister after independence. • He later served as President of the UN General Assembly and a judge of the International Court of Justice.

question: Who advocated separating Sindh from the Bombay Presidency?
answer: Sindhi Muslim leaders and the All-India Muslim League supported separation; Jinnah included separation of Sindh from Bombay among his constitutional demands in the Fourteen Points (1929).
facts: • Sindh became a separate province in 1936. • The issue was raised before the 1935 Government of India Act came into operation.

question: Who won the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
answer: France.
facts: • France defeated Croatia 4–2 in the final on 15 July 2018. • The tournament was hosted by Russia.

question: Who was President when Pakistan's 1956 Constitution came into force?
answer: Iskander Mirza.
facts: • Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956. • The 1956 Constitution established a parliamentary system and was abrogated in 1958.

question: When did Muhammad Ali Jinnah leave the Indian National Congress?
answer: He broke with Congress in 1920, around the Nagpur session in December.
facts: • Jinnah opposed Gandhi's mass non-cooperation approach. • He had joined the All-India Muslim League in 1913.

question: When was the Conquest of Makkah?
facts: • It took place in Ramadan. • The conquest followed the breakdown of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

question: Between whom was Mawakhat-e-Madinah established?
answer: Between the Muhajirun (migrants from Makkah) and the Ansar (helpers of Madinah).
facts: • The arrangement helped migrants establish social and economic support in Madinah. • Muhajirun means “those who migrated”; Ansar means “helpers”.

question: Who is known by the title “Asadullah”?
answer: Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) is commonly associated with this title.
facts: • “Asadullah” means “Lion of Allah”. • Hazrat Hamza (RA) is also called the Lion of Allah in traditional accounts.

question: When was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah born?
answer: 25 December 1876.
facts: • He was born in Karachi. • He died on 11 September 1948 and served as Pakistan's first Governor-General.

question: When was the Nehru Report published?
answer: 30 August 1928.
facts: • It was prepared under Motilal Nehru to propose constitutional reforms for British India. • Jinnah later presented his Fourteen Points in 1929 in response to the constitutional debate.

question: Which continent has historically been called the “Dark Continent”?
answer: Africa (a dated historical label, not a scientific description).
facts: • The phrase arose in European colonial-era writing and is now considered outdated. • Africa is the world's second-largest continent by area and population.

question: Is the Red Sea also known as the Gulf of Arabia?
answer: No. “Gulf of Arabia” is not a standard modern synonym for the Red Sea; a historic name is the Erythraean Sea.
facts: • The Red Sea lies between northeast Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. • It connects with the Gulf of Aden through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait.

question: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan?
answer: Bishkek.
facts: • Kyrgyzstan is a landlocked country in Central Asia. • Its currency is the som.

question: Who partitioned Bengal in 1905?
answer: Lord Curzon; the partition took effect in 1905, not 1913.
facts: • The partition was annulled in 1911. • The 1905 partition helped stimulate the Swadeshi Movement.

question: What is the length of Pakistan's coastline?
answer: About 1,046 km, according to Pakistan's Board of Investment.
facts: • Pakistan's coast lies along the Arabian Sea. • Major coastal areas include Karachi, the Makran coast and Gwadar.

question: What does “Badr” refer to, and what does the word mean?
answer: Badr is a settlement in present-day Saudi Arabia and the site of the Battle of Badr; the Arabic word is commonly glossed as “full moon”.
facts: • The battle took place in 2 AH (624 CE). • Badr lies southwest of Madinah.

question: Which country is the largest producer of carpets?
answer: This depends on whether the question means handmade carpets, machine-made carpets or value. Iran is famous for Persian handmade carpets, but “largest producer” is not a reliable single answer without a measure.
facts: • India and China are also major carpet producers and exporters. • For an exam, verify whether the syllabus specifically asks about handmade Persian carpets.

question: What is sin 90°?
facts: • On the unit circle, the sine of 90° is the y-coordinate at the top of the circle. • In radians, 90° = π/2.

question: In which year did Abdus Salam receive the Nobel Prize?
answer: 1979, in Physics.
facts: • He shared the prize with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg. • He was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate.

question: What is the capital of Sri Lanka?
answer: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital; Colombo is the largest city and major commercial centre.
facts: • Sri Lanka is an island country in the Indian Ocean. • Many quiz keys give Colombo, but the question should distinguish the legislative capital from the commercial centre.

question: What is the name of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border?
answer: The Durand Line.
facts: • It was agreed in 1893. • The boundary remains politically contentious in Afghanistan-Pakistan relations.

question: Who is commonly credited with providing an intellectual vision for a separate Muslim-majority state in South Asia?
answer: Allama Muhammad Iqbal is commonly credited with articulating an important vision in his Allahabad Address (1930); Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name “Pakistan” in 1933.
facts: • Iqbal delivered the Allahabad Address in December 1930. • Rahmat Ali published the “Now or Never” pamphlet in 1933.

question: What was Allama Iqbal's first Persian philosophical book?
answer: Asrar-e-Khudi, published in 1915.
facts: • The title is translated as “The Secrets of the Self”. • Bang-e-Dara, published in 1924, was his first major Urdu poetry collection.

question: When did Abu Bakr (RA) lead the Hajj, and when was Hajj made obligatory?
answer: Abu Bakr (RA) led the pilgrimage in 9 AH; many Islamic histories place the obligation of Hajj in 9 AH as well.
facts: • Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) performed his Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH. • Some references distinguish the date Hajj became obligatory from the first pilgrimage led by Abu Bakr.

question: What was the name of Hazrat Uthman ibn Affan's father?
answer: Affan ibn Abi al-As.
facts: • Hazrat Uthman (RA) was the third Rightly Guided Caliph. • He married two daughters of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) at different times, earning the honorific Dhun-Nurayn in Islamic tradition.

question: Which city is often described as one of Pakistan's oldest continuously inhabited cities?
answer: Multan is often described this way, but the claim to be the single oldest depends on the definition and evidence used.
facts: • Multan is known as the “City of Saints” because of its many Sufi shrines. • The Indus Valley Civilization sites, such as Mohenjo-daro, are much older archaeological settlements but were not continuously inhabited cities in the modern sense.

question: What is the currency of Türkiye (Turkey)?
answer: The Turkish lira.
facts: • Its currency code is TRY. • Ankara is Türkiye's capital; Istanbul is its largest city.

question: Which country is called the “Land of White Elephants”?
answer: Thailand.
facts: • The white elephant is culturally and historically associated with Thai royalty. • Thailand's capital is Bangkok.

question: Who was the first Caliph of Islam?
answer: Hazrat Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA).
facts: • He led the Muslim community from 632 to 634 CE. • He was succeeded by Hazrat Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA).

question: Who was the first Pakistani to travel to space?
answer: Namira Salim became the first Pakistani to travel to space as a private space traveller on Virgin Galactic in 2023, not 2009.
facts: • She flew on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 suborbital mission in October 2023. • Pakistan has not yet operated a government astronaut on an orbital space mission.

question: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
answer: Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-e-Azam).
facts: • He served from 14 August 1947 until his death on 11 September 1948. • “Governor-General” is different from a provincial governor.

question: What was the first major war between Pakistan and India over Kashmir?
answer: The Indo-Pakistani War of 1947–1948.
facts: • It began soon after the 1947 partition of British India. • A UN-arranged ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949.

question: When was the Tashkent Declaration signed?
answer: 10 January 1966.
facts: • It was signed by Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan. • It followed the 1965 Indo-Pakistani War.

question: When was the Badshahi Mosque built?
answer: It was commissioned by Aurangzeb and completed in 1673.
facts: • It is located in Lahore, opposite Lahore Fort. • It was one of the world's largest mosques at the time of its construction.

question: What is commonly listed as Pakistan's longest national highway?
answer: N-5 (National Highway 5).
facts: • It runs from Karachi through major cities toward Torkham. • The Karakoram Highway is internationally known for its high-altitude route, but it is not Pakistan's longest national highway.

question: How many idols were reportedly kept in the Kaaba before the Conquest of Makkah?
answer: Traditional Islamic accounts give 360 idols.
facts: • The idols were removed after the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH. • The Kaaba is in Masjid al-Haram in Makkah.

question: Which glacier is often listed as Pakistan's second-longest glacier after Siachen?
answer: Baltoro Glacier is often listed as the second-longest in Pakistan, though rankings depend on what is being measured.
facts: • Siachen Glacier is the longest glacier in the Karakoram region. • Baltoro Glacier lies in the Central Karakoram and provides access to Concordia and K2 trekking routes.

question: Who wrote the “Now or Never” pamphlet and when?
answer: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali published “Now or Never” in 1933.
facts: • The pamphlet advocated a separate Muslim homeland and used the name “Pakistan”. • Rahmat Ali was a student in Cambridge at the time.

question: When did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
answer: 30 September 1947.
facts: • The UN General Assembly admitted Pakistan by Resolution 108 (II). • Pakistan became a UN member shortly after independence.

question: When was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born?
answer: Commonly dated to around 570 or 571 CE, in the Year of the Elephant.
facts: • He was born in Makkah. • The exact Gregorian year is an estimate because contemporaneous date records are not precise.

question: Who is associated with the title “Atiq”?
answer: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is traditionally associated with the title “Atiq”.
facts: • He is best known by the title Al-Siddiq. • He was the first Caliph after Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

question: When was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
answer: 21 April 1526.
facts: • Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the battle. • The battle is conventionally associated with the establishment of Mughal rule in northern India.

question: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly?
answer: Rahila Hameed Khan Durrani.
facts: • She served as Speaker of the Balochistan Provincial Assembly. • A provincial assembly speaker presides over sessions and maintains order in the house.

question: Which country voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN in 1947?
answer: Afghanistan cast the sole vote against Pakistan's admission in the UN General Assembly vote.
facts: • Pakistan was admitted on 30 September 1947. • The General Assembly vote was 53 in favour, one against, with abstentions recorded in the historical table.

question: Which angel brought revelation to the Prophets?
answer: Angel Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him.
facts: • Jibril conveyed the Quranic revelation to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). • The Quran also refers to him as Ruh al-Amin and Ruh al-Qudus in relevant contexts.

question: What is the capital of Mongolia?
answer: Ulaanbaatar.
facts: • Mongolia is a landlocked country between Russia and China. • The name is also transliterated as Ulan Bator.

question: Where were the 2016 Summer Olympics held?
answer: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
facts: • The games took place from 5 to 21 August 2016. • It was the first Summer Olympics held in South America.

question: When did Jinnah present the Delhi Proposals?
answer: The Delhi Muslim Proposals were presented in 1927; the “Delhi Pact of 1916” wording is incorrect or confuses them with the Lucknow Pact of 1916.
facts: • Jinnah made the Delhi Proposals as an attempt at Hindu-Muslim constitutional agreement. • The Lucknow Pact was agreed by the Congress and Muslim League in 1916.

question: There are 48 heads and 140 legs among hens and cows. How many hens are there?
answer: 26 hens.
facts: • Let hens = h and cows = c: h + c = 48, 2h + 4c = 140. • Solving gives c = 22 and h = 26.

question: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?
facts: • It was a truce between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh of Makkah. • The treaty preceded the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

question: For what did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Prize?
answer: The Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, for her struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education.
facts: • She shared the prize with Kailash Satyarthi. • Malala was the youngest Nobel Prize laureate at the time of the award.

question: When did the Khilafat Movement begin?
answer: It began in 1919 and continued into the early 1920s.
facts: • It sought to preserve the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I. • It overlapped with the Non-Cooperation Movement in British India.

question: Complete the sentence: “Ali was born ___ 20 August 1997.”
answer: on.
facts: • Use “on” with a specific date: “on 20 August 1997”. • Use “in” with a month or year: “in August”, “in 1997”.

question: What was the approximate Muslim force at the Battle of Badr?
answer: About 313 Muslims, according to the traditional Islamic account.
facts: • The battle took place in 2 AH (624 CE). • The Muslim force was much smaller than the Quraysh force in traditional accounts.

question: What is Sahifa al-Sadiqa?
answer: An early written collection of hadith associated with Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As; it is often called Sahifa al-Sadiqa.
facts: • It is sometimes described in general-knowledge books as the first hadith book, but “first” depends on how one defines a book or written collection. • Early hadith material was written down during the first Islamic centuries.

question: Which international organization did Pakistan join as a full member in 2017?
answer: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).
facts: • Pakistan became a full member in June 2017 at the Astana summit. • Pakistan had held SCO observer status from 2005.

question: Which country is commonly said to have been the first to recognize Pakistan?
answer: Iran is commonly cited in Pakistani general-knowledge sources as the first country to recognize Pakistan.
facts: • Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947. • The wording “first to recognize” can vary by whether a source means formal recognition, diplomatic relations or earliest bilateral mission.

question: Who was the first muezzin of Islam?
answer: Hazrat Bilal ibn Rabah (RA).
facts: • A muezzin calls Muslims to prayer through the adhan. • Bilal (RA) was an early Muslim who endured persecution before the Hijrah.

question: Which key opens spell check in Microsoft Word?
facts: • F7 opens spelling and grammar review in many desktop versions of Word. • Shortcuts may differ by operating system or customized keyboard settings.

question: What role did the World Bank play in the Indus Waters Treaty?
answer: The World Bank brokered/facilitated the treaty; it was signed by India and Pakistan in 1960.
facts: • The treaty allocates use of the Indus river system waters between the two countries. • It was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.

question: What percentage of Pakistan's land area is classified as forest?
answer: The World Bank's forest-area indicator reports about 4.6% for Pakistan in 2023; the submitted 1.91% figure is not the current World Bank measure.
facts: • Forest-area percentages differ by definition, inventory and year. • Use a named source and reference year in exam notes instead of mixing estimates.

question: During whose caliphate was the Battle of Yamama fought?
answer: During the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), in 11 AH (632–633 CE).
facts: • The battle was fought against forces associated with Musaylima. • The heavy loss of Quran reciters is traditionally linked to the decision to collect Quranic material.

question: Where are Pakistan's major coal reserves found?
answer: Thar in Sindh holds Pakistan's largest coal resource; coal is also found in Balochistan, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
facts: • The Thar coalfield lies in Tharparkar District. • Resource estimates and extractable reserves are different measures.

question: In which Hijri year was zakat made obligatory?
answer: Commonly dated to 2 AH for formal obligatory zakat.
facts: • Zakat is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. • Its rate and eligibility depend on the type of wealth and the relevant conditions.

question: How many daughters did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have?
answer: Four: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with them).
facts: • They are commonly identified as the daughters of the Prophet and Khadijah (RA). • Fatimah (RA) was the youngest daughter in the traditional account.

question: Which prophet is mentioned most often by name in the Quran?
answer: Prophet Musa (Moses), peace be upon him; a commonly cited count is 136 mentions.
facts: • Counts can vary with counting method and name forms. • His story appears across many Surahs, including Al-Baqarah, Al-A'raf and Ta-Ha.

question: What is the integral of cot x?
answer: ∫ cot x dx = ln|sin x| + C.
facts: • cot x = cos x / sin x. • The constant C represents any constant of integration.

question: Who was the mother of Prophet Ishaq (Isaac), peace be upon him?
answer: Sarah (Sara), according to the Biblical and Islamic historical tradition.
facts: • Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) was his father. • Prophet Ismail (Ishmael) was Ibrahim's son through Hajar in Islamic tradition.

question: Which pass connects Chitral with Afghanistan?
answer: Dorah Pass (also spelled Dorah/Dorah Pass).
facts: • It connects the Chitral area with Afghanistan's Badakhshan region. • High passes in the Hindu Kush may be snowbound or difficult to cross seasonally.

question: In which expedition did the Muslims return without a major battle?
answer: The Expedition of Tabuk (9 AH) is commonly given in this type of MCQ; there was no full-scale battle.
facts: • Tabuk lies in present-day northwestern Saudi Arabia. • The expedition took place during a difficult period of heat and scarcity.

question: Which planet is nearest to Earth?
answer: Venus can come closest to Earth at its closest approach; Mercury is the nearest planet on average over time. The question must specify the definition.
facts: • School MCQs commonly expect Venus for closest approach. • Astronomers distinguish minimum approach distance from average distance over time.

question: Pakistan has opposed India's unconditional inclusion in which group?
answer: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG).
facts: • Pakistan has advocated a criteria-based approach to membership. • The NSG is a group of nuclear supplier states that coordinates controls on nuclear exports.

question: How is an earthquake's magnitude measured?
answer: Modern earthquake magnitude is commonly reported using the Moment Magnitude scale (Mw); the Richter scale is a historical/local magnitude scale.
facts: • Magnitude estimates earthquake size; intensity describes observed effects at a place. • The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale measures shaking effects and damage.

question: When is friction between a tyre and the road at its maximum useful level?
answer: Near the limit of static friction, just before the tyre begins to skid; “hard braking” alone is not a precise scientific answer.
facts: • Locked, sliding tyres usually have less friction than tyres rolling near the peak grip threshold. • Anti-lock braking systems help prevent wheel lockup and maintain steering control.

question: What are ambassadors of Commonwealth countries to one another commonly called?
answer: High Commissioners.
facts: • A High Commissioner heads a diplomatic mission between Commonwealth member countries. • The mission is called a High Commission rather than an embassy.

question: What is Earth's circumference?
answer: About 40,075 km at the equator.
facts: • The meridional/polar circumference is about 40,008 km. • Earth is an oblate spheroid, so its circumference varies by direction.

question: What are the main functions of the IMF?
answer: To promote international monetary cooperation and exchange stability, support trade and growth, monitor economies, and provide financing to members facing balance-of-payments problems.
facts: • The IMF is not simply a body that balances supply and demand of currencies. • Its headquarters are in Washington, D.C.

question: What is the Pentagon?
answer: The headquarters of the United States Department of Defense, in Arlington, Virginia.
facts: • Its five-sided building gave it the name “Pentagon”. • It is located across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C.

question: What is the capital of Sierra Leone?
answer: Freetown.
facts: • Sierra Leone is in West Africa on the Atlantic coast. • English is the official language.

question: Who led the opposing Meccan force at the Battle of Uhud?
answer: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb was the principal leader of the Meccan force; Khalid ibn al-Walid commanded its cavalry.
facts: • The Battle of Uhud occurred in 3 AH (625 CE). • Khalid ibn al-Walid later accepted Islam and became a major Muslim commander.

question: Who was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in Pakistan?
answer: Justice Syeda Tahira Safdar, appointed Chief Justice of the Balochistan High Court in 2018.
facts: • She was the first woman to head a Pakistani High Court. • She retired in 2019.

question: What is the space between a document margin and the start of a paragraph called?
answer: Indentation, when referring to the paragraph's inset from the margin; spacing before a paragraph is a different formatting setting.
facts: • First-line and hanging indents are common paragraph formats. • In Word, paragraph spacing controls the vertical gap before or after paragraphs.

question: What is cutting away unwanted parts of an image called?
answer: Cropping.
facts: • Cropping changes the visible bounds of an image. • Cropping differs from resizing, which changes displayed or pixel dimensions.

question: Which Microsoft Word feature creates decorative text?
answer: WordArt.
facts: • WordArt applies stylized effects to text. • It is useful for titles and decorative headings, not usually long body text.

question: In which country was the 1955 Bandung Conference held, which helped inspire the Non-Aligned Movement?
answer: Indonesia.
facts: • The conference was held in Bandung in April 1955. • The Non-Aligned Movement was formally established at Belgrade in 1961.

question: What minerals does the Saindak project produce?
answer: Copper and gold, with silver also recovered.
facts: • The project is in Chagai District, Balochistan. • Saindak is a copper-gold mine and processing project.

question: What type of legislature does Pakistan have at the federal level?
answer: Bicameral.
facts: • Parliament consists of the National Assembly and the Senate. • “Bicameral” means two chambers; each province has a single provincial assembly.

question: What is Pakistan's largest operating oil refinery?
answer: PARCO's Mid-Country Refinery (MCR), near Mahmoodkot, with a reported capacity of 120,000 barrels per day.
facts: • PARCO stands for Pak-Arab Refinery Limited. • The company's MCR is described by PARCO as Pakistan's largest operating refinery.

question: What is the purpose of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
answer: To administer trade agreements, provide a forum for trade negotiations, help settle trade disputes and review members' trade policies.
facts: • The WTO was established in 1995. • Its headquarters are in Geneva, Switzerland.

question: Which vitamin supports wound healing?
answer: Vitamin C is important for normal collagen formation and wound healing; protein and other nutrients also matter.
facts: • Vitamin C is also called ascorbic acid. • Vitamin C deficiency can impair collagen synthesis and wound repair.

question: What is a major immediate energy source for an athlete?
answer: Carbohydrates are a major readily available energy source, especially during high-intensity exercise.
facts: • Carbohydrates are stored as glycogen in muscles and the liver. • Fat and, to a smaller extent, protein also contribute to energy metabolism.

question: A book costs Rs 500 and is sold for Rs 700. What is the profit percentage?
facts: • Profit = 700 − 500 = Rs 200. • Profit percentage = 200 ÷ 500 × 100 = 40%.

question: When did Pakistan become a member of the UN?
answer: 30 September 1947.
facts: • This duplicates Question 100 in the submitted list; the verified answer is the same. • Pakistan was admitted through UN General Assembly Resolution 108 (II).

question: Which battle is called Jang-e-Furqan?
answer: The Battle of Badr.
facts: • It took place in 2 AH (624 CE). • The word Furqan means a criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.

question: Evaluate 2 + 2 ÷ 2.
facts: • Apply division before addition: 2 + (2 ÷ 2) = 2 + 1. • This is an order-of-operations question.

question: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud?
answer: About 70 Muslims were martyred; 85 is not the standard figure.
facts: • The battle occurred in 3 AH (625 CE). • Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib (RA) was among those martyred.

question: What has historically been Pakistan's largest broad source category for electricity generation?
answer: Thermal power has historically supplied the largest combined share, but the leading source and percentages vary by year as hydel, nuclear and renewables change.
facts: • Thermal includes electricity generated from fuels such as gas, coal and oil. • For a current-affairs test, use the latest NEPRA/Pakistan Energy Yearbook data and its reference year.

question: In which direction is Iran from Pakistan?
answer: West.
facts: • Iran shares a border with Pakistan's Balochistan province. • Pakistan also borders Afghanistan, China and India, as well as the Arabian Sea.

question: How many Muslims are traditionally reported to have been martyred at the Battle of Yamama?
answer: About 70 Quran reciters are commonly reported to have been martyred, though accounts differ in the total number of Muslim casualties.
facts: • The Battle of Yamama took place during Abu Bakr's caliphate. • The loss of reciters is linked in tradition to the early collection of Quranic material.

question: When was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's “Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind” (“The Causes of the Indian Revolt”) published?
answer: The essay was written/published in 1858; 10 May 1857 is the date the uprising began at Meerut, not the publication date.
facts: • Sir Syed argued that British policies and lack of communication contributed to the uprising. • An English translation appeared later.

question: On what date was the Objectives Resolution introduced in the Constituent Assembly?
answer: 7 March 1949; it was passed on 12 March 1949.
facts: • Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved the resolution. • Question 1 asks about the passing date; this item asks the introduction date.

question: Which pronoun can replace the singular noun “school” in a sentence?
answer: It, when the school is referred to as a thing or institution.
facts: • Example: “The school is old. It needs repairs.” • Use “they” when referring to schools in the plural.

question: What does SAFTA stand for?
answer: South Asian Free Trade Area.
facts: • The SAFTA agreement was signed in 2004 and came into force in 2006. • It is associated with the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC).

question: How many Muslims were initially present at the Battle of Uhud?
answer: About 1,000 initially; around 300 withdrew before the battle, leaving about 700.
facts: • The Battle of Uhud took place in 3 AH (625 CE). • The Muslims faced a larger Meccan force.

question: How many types of articles are there in English grammar?
answer: Two types: definite (the) and indefinite (a/an). There are three common forms: a, an and the.
facts: • Use “a” before a consonant sound and “an” before a vowel sound. • “The” is used when the noun is specific or identifiable.

question: What does IMF stand for?
answer: International Monetary Fund.
facts: • The IMF was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and began operations in 1945. • Its headquarters are in Washington, D.C.

question: Who founded the Urdu Defence Association?
answer: Mohsin-ul-Mulk is commonly credited in general-knowledge references with organizing the Urdu Defence Association in 1900.
facts: • It was established amid the Urdu-Hindi controversy in the United Provinces. • Always distinguish it from the Anjuman-e-Taraqqi-e-Urdu, a separate Urdu-language organization.

question: How many times is the name Jibril explicitly mentioned in the Quran?
answer: Three times: Quran 2:97, 2:98 and 66:4.
facts: • References to Ruh al-Qudus or Ruh al-Amin are separate expressions and are not counted as the name Jibril. • The answer depends on counting the explicit name, not all possible titles.

question: Mount Olympus is in which country?
answer: Greece.
facts: • Mount Olympus is Greece's highest mountain. • In Greek mythology, it was regarded as the home of the gods.

question: Who was the last prophet sent to the Children of Israel, according to Islamic belief?
answer: Prophet Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, is commonly described as the last prophet sent to Bani Israel before Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
facts: • Prophet Isa was born to Maryam (Mary), according to Islamic belief. • Muslims regard Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as the final prophet for all humanity.

question: What was France's currency before the euro?
answer: The French franc.
facts: • France adopted the euro for electronic transactions in 1999 and euro banknotes/coins in 2002. • One euro replaced 6.55957 French francs at the fixed conversion rate.

question: What is one tenth of 90?
facts: • One tenth means divide by 10. • 90 ÷ 10 = 9.

question: What is one tenth of 120?
facts: • One tenth means 10% of the number. • 120 ÷ 10 = 12.

question: Who enslaved Hazrat Bilal (RA) before his freedom?
answer: Umayyah ibn Khalaf.
facts: • Bilal (RA) was persecuted in Makkah for accepting Islam. • Abu Bakr (RA) purchased and freed him according to traditional Islamic accounts.

question: Where do articles usually appear in an English noun phrase?
answer: Before a noun or noun phrase, often before any adjective: “a book”, “the old house”.
facts: • The articles are a, an and the. • Some noun phrases do not use an article, such as many proper names and plural/uncountable nouns in general statements.

question: What is the literal meaning of Islam?
answer: Submission or surrender to Allah; in Islamic usage, willing submission to God.
facts: • The word is related to the Arabic root s-l-m, associated with peace and submission. • A Muslim is one who submits to Allah.

question: Of 1,500 students, 1,200 are present. What percentage is present?
facts: • Percentage = 1,200 ÷ 1,500 × 100. • Absent students = 300, or 20%.

question: Of 500 students, 340 are present. What percentage is absent?
facts: • Absent students = 500 − 340 = 160. • Absent percentage = 160 ÷ 500 × 100 = 32%.

question: What does Akhuwat/Mawakhat mean?
answer: Brotherhood; Mawakhat particularly refers to the brothering of the Muhajirun and Ansar in Madinah.
facts: • Akhuwat is also the name of a Pakistani microfinance/social-support organization. • The Arabic root conveys brotherhood/fraternity.

question: What was Hudaybiyyah?
answer: A place near Makkah where the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded in 6 AH (628 CE).
facts: • The treaty allowed a truce between the Muslims and Quraysh. • The site is associated with the Prophet's attempted pilgrimage from Madinah.

question: Who is associated with the residency at Ziarat?
answer: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
facts: • The Quaid-e-Azam Residency is in Ziarat, Balochistan. • Jinnah stayed there in 1948 during his final illness.

question: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the Harb al-Fijar?
answer: Some traditional accounts give about 15 years, but reports vary; treat the age as approximate.
facts: • Harb al-Fijar refers to a series of conflicts among Arabian tribes before Islam. • The Prophet is reported to have accompanied relatives but not fought as a principal combatant.

question: Who produced the first complete, published Urdu translation of the Quran?
answer: Shah Abdul Qadir's Urdu translation, published in 1829, is commonly credited as the first complete published Urdu translation; Maulana Aashiq Ilahi Merathi was not the first.
facts: • Earlier Urdu translations or partial translations may have existed but were unpublished or did not survive. • This correction follows the linguistic-history discussion published in Dawn by Rauf Parekh.

question: What is the McMahon Line?
answer: A line drawn in the eastern sector of the disputed China-India boundary under the 1914 Simla Convention; it is not the name of the entire China-India border.
facts: • India accepts the line as its boundary in the eastern sector; China disputes it. • The line was named after British diplomat Henry McMahon.

question: According to a commonly cited hadith, what is the jihad of women?
answer: A righteous Hajj is described in a hadith as the best or equivalent form of jihad for women; “Hijab” is not the standard answer to this specific question.
facts: • The exact wording and interpretation depend on the hadith report and context. • This is a religious-text question, so use the wording in the prescribed syllabus or reliable hadith reference.

question: They are three brothers. Ali is ___ of the three.
answer: the cleverest.
facts: • For three or more people/things, the superlative form is commonly used. • “Cleverer” is comparative; “cleverest” is superlative.

question: Complete the sentence: “He served us ___ breakfast.”
answer: “a good breakfast” is grammatical; “He served us a good breakfast.”
facts: • “Breakfast” is usually uncountable, but it can take “a” when referring to a particular meal or type of breakfast. • “He served us breakfast” is also correct without an article.

question: Where are Pakistan's famous salt mines located?
answer: Khewra, in Punjab.
facts: • Khewra Salt Mine is in the Salt Range near Pind Dadan Khan. • It is among the world's well-known salt mines and is a major tourist site.

question: When was the Conquest of Khaybar?
facts: • Khaybar is an oasis region north of Madinah. • The event followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

question: For what purpose is Salat al-Istisqa offered?
answer: To pray for rain during drought or shortage of rain.
facts: • It is a congregational prayer in Islamic practice. • The word Istisqa means seeking water/rain.

question: When was the Jinnah Antarctic Research Station established?
answer: 18 January 1991.
facts: • The station was established during Pakistan's Antarctic expedition. • Pakistan later became an associate member of the Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research in 1992.

question: When was the Lahore Resolution adopted?
answer: 23 March 1940.
facts: • It was adopted at the All-India Muslim League session in Lahore. • It is also called the Pakistan Resolution; 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day.

question: In which year did World War I end?
answer: 1918; the Armistice was signed on 11 November 1918.
facts: • The war began in 1914. • The Treaty of Versailles with Germany was signed in 1919.

question: What is the world's largest island?
answer: Greenland.
facts: • Australia is classified as a continent, not an island in the usual school-geography convention. • Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

question: What does OPEC stand for?
answer: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
facts: • OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960. • Its headquarters are in Vienna, Austria.

question: On which river is Diamer-Bhasha Dam being built?
answer: The Indus River.
facts: • The project is in the Gilgit-Baltistan/Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region. • Its aims include water storage, irrigation support and hydropower generation.

question: When was the Battle of Uhud fought?
facts: • The battle took place near Mount Uhud, north of Madinah. • It followed the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.

question: Where is the Jinnah Antarctic Research Station located?
answer: In East Antarctica, in the Queen Maud Land region as commonly described.
facts: • It was established in January 1991. • It supports Pakistan's scientific work in Antarctica.

question: Who is the only Companion of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) mentioned by name in the Quran?
answer: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA).
facts: • He is named in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:37). • Do not confuse him with Zayd ibn Thabit, the scribe associated with the collection of Quranic material.

question: The FSB is the security agency of which country?
answer: Russia.
facts: • FSB stands for Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation. • It is a domestic security and counterintelligence service, not simply a foreign intelligence agency.

question: Who said of the Prophet (PBUH), “His character was the Quran”?
answer: Hazrat Aisha (RA), describing the Prophet's character when asked about it.
facts: • The report is found in hadith collections, including Sahih Muslim. • The statement describes his character as embodying Quranic teachings.

question: Who is Pakistan's Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue?
answer: Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb (as listed by the Finance Division on 14 October 2026).
facts: • This is a date-sensitive office-holder question; check the Finance Division website close to the exam. • He was appointed Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue in March 2024.

question: Who is known by the title “Ruhullah”?
answer: Prophet Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, in Islamic tradition.
facts: • The title means “Spirit of Allah” and is used as an honorific in Islamic tradition. • Islamic belief distinguishes this honorific from any claim that Isa is divine.

question: To which prophet was the Zabur revealed?
answer: Prophet Dawud (David), peace be upon him.
facts: • Zabur is commonly identified with the Psalms in comparative religious studies. • Dawud is also known as a king and prophet in Islamic tradition.

question: What is the approximate length of the Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir?
answer: About 740 km, according to a commonly cited estimate.
facts: • The LoC separates areas administered by India and Pakistan in the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. • It is not an internationally recognized final border settlement.

question: On which river is Mangla Dam built?
answer: The Jhelum River.
facts: • Mangla Dam is near Mirpur in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. • It was completed in 1967 and is used for water storage, irrigation and hydropower.

question: Which province is known as Babul Islam?
answer: Sindh.
facts: • The phrase means “Gateway of Islam”. • Muhammad bin Qasim conquered parts of Sindh in 711–712 CE.

question: Bari Doab lies between which rivers?
answer: The Ravi and Beas rivers.
facts: • “Doab” means a tract of land between two rivers. • Bari Doab is in the Punjab region of the Indus basin.

question: Which Surahs are called Al-Mu'awwidhatayn?
answer: Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah An-Nas (114).
facts: • The two Surahs are recited for seeking Allah's protection. • The spelling is commonly transliterated as Al-Mu'awwidhatayn.

question: Which Surah was recited before Najashi by Ja'far ibn Abi Talib?
answer: Surah Maryam.
facts: • Ja'far recited passages about Maryam and Isa (peace be upon them) in the traditional account. • This occurred during the early Muslim migration to Abyssinia.

question: Which well-known body of water is famous for its very high salinity?
answer: The Dead Sea, technically a hypersaline lake rather than a true sea.
facts: • It lies between Jordan and the West Bank/Israel region. • Some smaller hypersaline lakes can have higher salinity, so “most saline water on Earth” is not universally true.

question: Which parties signed the Lucknow Pact?
answer: The Indian National Congress and the All-India Muslim League in 1916.
facts: • The pact supported constitutional reforms and separate electorates for Muslims. • Jinnah played an important role in the negotiations.

question: Which country has the world's longest written national constitution?
answer: India is commonly credited with having the longest written constitution of any sovereign country.
facts: • It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950. • The Constitution of India has been amended many times.

question: In which year did Shah Waliullah die?
facts: • He was a major Islamic scholar and reformer in South Asia. • He translated the Quran into Persian; his son Shah Abdul Qadir later produced a major Urdu translation.

question: In which mountain range is Siachen Glacier located?
answer: The eastern Karakoram Range.
facts: • Siachen lies in the eastern Karakoram in the broader Kashmir region. • It is often described as the longest glacier outside the polar regions, depending on classification.

question: A train travels at 120 miles per hour. How far does it travel in 12 minutes?
answer: 24 miles, which is about 38.6 km.
facts: • 12 minutes = 0.2 hour. • Distance = speed × time = 120 × 0.2 = 24 miles.

question: Which Surah is traditionally called the “Heart of the Quran”?
answer: Surah Ya-Sin (Surah 36), in popular Islamic tradition; the authenticity/grading of the specific hadith wording is debated.
facts: • It contains 83 verses in the common Hafs numbering. • For strict hadith questions, distinguish popular titles from reports established as authentic.

question: If yesterday was Monday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
answer: Thursday.
facts: • If yesterday was Monday, today is Tuesday. • Tomorrow is Wednesday; the day after tomorrow is Thursday.
